definitions.explanation: Describes something of less than average size. The opposite of {大|おお}きい (big). Used for physical dimensions of objects, spaces, and living things.
When describing voices or sounds, {小|ちい}さい means quiet or soft. {小|ちい}さい{声|こえ} means a quiet/soft voice.

examples.japanese: このカバンは{小|ちい}さいです。
{小|ちい}さい{子供|こども}がいます。
examples.english: There is a small child. / I have a small child.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さい{声|こえ}で{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: Please speak in a quiet voice.

notes: {小|ちい}さい is an i-adjective. Like {大|おお}きい, it has a special attributive form {小|ちい}さな that can only be used directly before nouns. Both {小|ちい}さい{猫|ねこ} and {小|ちい}さな{猫|ねこ} mean 'small cat.' Conjugation: {小|ちい}さくない (negative), {小|ちい}さかった (past).
